title: Learning while doing
sub: The last film of The new skills, the first series of Leading data people: learning on the job. Skills grow fastest on the real work, a small step at a time, beside someone who knows; teaching what you learn makes it last, and spreads it; and learning needs time kept for it. A new analyst learns the team's project beside a colleague, teaches the team what she learned, and by June nobody is the only one who can run a job.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's sunlit plaster: the team's rooms in daylight, with sheets pinned to the wall. Its colours mean the same in every film: blue is plans and design (the learning time in the calendar), orange is data (the sensors' counts), green is something done or shared (a small change, reviewed; a second name on a job), and amber a risk (a job only one person can run, and Angicos's problem).
